g.text: Explore the structure of a complete flower

text.tspan: Match each label from the word bank to the correct part of the flower using the
numbered target areas and arrows as a guide.
1. Study the coloured flower diagram in the centre.
2. Each dashed box marks a target area for a label.
3. Use the arrows to see which structure each box refers to.
4. In a printed or digital activity, you would drag labels from
the word bank into these boxes.
5. Here, imagine where each label would go, then tap
Hint or Check Answer to reveal guidance.
Pollen grains are produced in the anther (part of the stamen).
During pollination, pollen is transferred to the sticky stigma
at the top of the pistil. A pollen tube grows down the style
to reach the ovary, where fertilisation of ovules takes place.
Pollinators (such as insects or wind) help move pollen from
anther to stigma. This enables seeds and fruit to develop.

g.text: Word bank andmdash; imagine dragging each label into the matching target box:
Hint: Look for colour and position clues

text.tspan: • Petals are usually the large, colourful structures that attract pollinators.
• Sepals are green and sit below the petals, supporting the base of the flower.
• The stamen is the male part of the flower: each one has a slender
filament with an anther on top that makes pollen.
• The central female structure is the pistil, made up of:
andndash; a sticky stigma at the top,
andndash; the slender style, and
andndash; the swollen ovary at the base.
• The receptacle is the thickened part of the stem that holds all
flower parts together at the base.
Compare your imagined placements to this key:
1. Top-left box andrarr; Petal (large coloured structures).
2. Left-middle box (above) andrarr; Style (slender stalk of the pistil).
3. Left-middle box (below) andrarr; Stigma (sticky tip of the pistil).
4. Left-lower box andrarr; Sepal (green leaf-like parts).
5. Left-bottom box andrarr; Receptacle (base where parts attach).
6. Top-right box andrarr; Stamen (whole male structure).
7. Upper-right box andrarr; Anther (pollen-producing tip).
8. Middle-right box andrarr; Pistil (entire female structure).
9. Lower-right box andrarr; Filament (slender stalk holding anther).
10. Lowest-right box andrarr; Ovary (swollen base containing ovules).
If you matched most of these correctly, you have a strong
understanding of basic flower anatomy.
This SVG simulates a drag-and-drop exercise without scripts.
To "reset" the activity:
• Clear any notes or written answers you have made.
• Look back at the main diagram and cover the word bank
with your hand or a piece of paper.
• Try to recall and place each label again from memory.
On a printed worksheet or interactive worksheet builder,
the same layout could be used for true drag-and-drop practice.
